en: one's own views; good grasp of something

examples.en: He really knows his way around cooking.
My father is quite an expert at baduk.

examples.ko: 커피에 일가견이 있는 친구에게 추천을 부탁했어요.
examples.en: I asked a friend who knows a lot about coffee for a recommendation.

examples.ko: 언니는 옷 고르는 데 일가견이 있어요.
examples.en: My older sister has a real eye for picking out clothes.

examples.ko: 이 분야에 일가견을 가진 전문가를 만났어요.
examples.en: I met an expert with deep insight into this field.

examples.ko: 여행 계획 짜는 일에는 제가 일가견이 있어요.
examples.en: When it comes to planning trips, I have a knack for it.

explain: '잘하다'나 '잘 알다'보다 자기만의 안목과 실력이 인정될 만하다는 느낌이에요. 거의 '~에 일가견이 있다' 꼴로 쓰고, 자기 자신에게 쓰면 조금 으스대는 느낌일 수 있어요.

phrases.en: be very knowledgeable about; have a good eye for
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 분야를 오래 접해서 자기만의 안목이 있다는 뜻으로, '일가견'만 따로는 잘 안 쓰고 이 꼴로 굳어 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means someone has a well-developed eye for a field after long experience. '일가견' is rarely used alone and is fixed in this phrase.
phrases.en_equiv: know a thing or two about

explain_en: Compared with '잘하다' or '잘 알다', it suggests you have your own discerning eye and skill that others would recognize. It is almost always used as '~에 일가견이 있다', and using it about yourself can sound a little boastful.

examples.ko: 일신상의 사정으로 이번 달까지만 일할 거예요.
examples.en: For personal reasons, I will only work until the end of this month.

examples.ko: 일신상 문제 때문에 오늘 모임에 못 가요.
examples.en: I can't go to today's meeting because of a personal matter.
Something difficult came up in my personal life, so I took a leave of absence.

examples.ko: 일신상에 문제가 있어서 이번 대회는 쉬기로 했어요.
examples.en: Because of a personal problem, I decided to sit out this competition.
I only wrote 'personal reasons' on my resignation letter.

examples.ko: 일신상 이유라고 하면 보통 더 묻지 않아요.
examples.en: When someone says it's for personal reasons, people usually don't ask more.

explain: '개인적인'을 격식 있게 말하는 표현으로, 회사나 서류에서 '일신상의 이유/사유/사정'이라고 많이 써요. 자세한 이유를 말하고 싶지 않을 때도 쓰지요. 친구와 말할 때는 '개인적인 일'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I can't attend the meeting for personal reasons.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자세한 이유를 말하지 않고 정중하게 거절할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to politely decline without giving details.

phrases.en: That person left the company for personal reasons.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사 서류나 공지에서 자주 보는 격식 있는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal phrase often seen in company documents and notices.

phrases.example: 개인적인 일이 있어서 오늘 먼저 갈게요.
phrases.en: I have something personal to take care of, so I'll leave early today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 동료와 말할 때 '일신상' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy, casual alternative to 일신상 when talking to friends or colleagues.

explain_en: It is a formal way of saying 'personal', commonly seen at work and in documents as '일신상의 이유/사유/사정'. It is also used when you don't want to give the details. With friends you would say '개인적인 일'.

en: student retaking the college entrance exam

examples.ko: 올해 재수생이 된 형이 학원에 다녀요.
examples.en: My older brother, who became a retaker this year, goes to a cram school.

examples.ko: 재수생은 공부 시간 관리가 정말 중요해요.
examples.en: For retakers, managing study time is really important.

examples.ko: 재수생으로 지내는 동안 친구들과 연락이 뜸해졌어요.
examples.en: While I was a retaker, I kept in touch with my friends less.

examples.ko: 내 사촌은 작년에 재수생 생활을 하고 올해 합격했어요.
examples.en: My cousin lived as a retaker last year and passed this year.

examples.ko: 재수생들을 위한 상담 프로그램이 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new counseling program for retakers has been created.

examples.ko: 재수생인데도 매일 웃으며 공부하는 친구가 대단해요.
examples.en: My friend studies with a smile every day even as a retaker, which is impressive.

explain: 대학 입시에서 한 번 떨어지거나 결과에 만족하지 못해 다시 준비하는 사람이에요. 줄여서 '재수'라고 하고, '재수하다'는 동사예요. 한 번 더 하면 '삼수생'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: My older brother is repeating the exam year now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '재수생'을 줄인 말로, 입시를 다시 준비하는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Short for 재수생; refers to preparing for the exam again.

phrases.en: I failed the exam, so I decided to try again next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재수생이 되어 다시 준비하는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb for becoming a 재수생 and preparing again.

phrases.en: This year I'm on my third attempt at the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재수생보다 한 번 더 도전하는 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Someone on one more attempt than a 재수생.

explain_en: It refers to a person who fails or is unsatisfied with a university entrance exam and prepares again. It is shortened to '재수', and '재수하다' is the verb. Someone who does it one more time is called a '삼수생'.

en: to hold a post; to be employed

examples.ko: 저는 이 회사에 십 년째 재직하고 있어요.
examples.en: I have been employed at this company for ten years.
He is a teacher who once worked at our school.
I learned a lot while I was employed there.

examples.ko: 재직할 때 만난 사람들과 아직 연락해요.
examples.en: I still keep in touch with the people I met while working there.
Before joining the university, I worked at a research institute.
Working here, I met good people.

explain: 어떤 직장에 속해서 일하고 있을 때 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. '일하다'는 어디서나 쓰지만 '재직하다'는 서류나 소개에서 '재직 증명서', '재직 중'처럼 써요. 직장을 그만두면 '퇴직하다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 저는 현재 이 회사에 재직 중이에요.
phrases.en: I currently work at this company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 그 직장에 있다는 뜻으로 서류나 소개에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you are currently employed there; used in documents and introductions.

phrases.en: The bank asked me to submit a certificate of employment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직장에 다닌다는 것을 증명하는 서류예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A document proving you work at a company.

phrases.en: My older sister works at a hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 덜 딱딱하고 일하는 곳을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A little less stiff, often used to say where one works.

explain_en: It is a formal word for being employed by an organization. '일하다' works everywhere, but '재직하다' appears in documents and introductions, as in '재직 증명서' (employment certificate) and '재직 중' (currently employed). When you leave the job, it becomes '퇴직하다'.

dis.h: formal: hold a post at an organization
gh: work on a task, project or craft
work at a set workplace during duty hours
everyday general word for working or doing a job

p.s: 아버지는 이 회사에 십 년째 재직하고 있다.
p.o: 아버지는 이 회사에 십 년째 근무하고 있다.
p.n: 재직하다 stresses being employed in a position and is formal and written. 근무하다 stresses the actual working.

en: to be enrolled; to be a student

examples.en: I'm currently enrolled in university.
My younger sibling is enrolled in high school.
I received a scholarship while I was enrolled.

examples.ko: 그는 대학교에 재학할 때 유학을 다녀왔어요.
examples.en: He went abroad to study while he was in university.

examples.ko: 이 학교에 재학 중인 학생은 도서관을 무료로 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: Students currently enrolled at this school can use the library for free.

examples.ko: 재학생이 아니면 학생 할인을 못 받아요.
examples.en: If you aren't a current student, you can't get the student discount.

explain: 학교에 다니고 있는 상태를 서류나 소개에서 말할 때 써요. 일상 말로는 '다니다'가 자연스러워요. '재학생', '재학 중', '재학 증명서'로 자주 나오고, 졸업했으면 '졸업생', 쉬고 있으면 '휴학 중'이에요.

phrases.en: I am currently enrolled in university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 학교에 다니는 상태를 서류나 소개에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in documents or introductions for the current state of attending school.

phrases.example: 재학생은 도서관을 무료로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Enrolled students can use the library for free.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 학교에 다니는 학생을 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for a student who currently attends the school.

phrases.en: I got a certificate of enrollment from school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에 다닌다는 것을 증명하는 서류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A document proving that you attend the school.

explain_en: Formal; being currently enrolled at a school or university (대학교에 재학하다). Use it for the state of attending school in documents and introductions. In everyday speech 다니다 sounds more natural. It appears as '재학생', '재학 중', and '재학 증명서'; graduates are 졸업생 and those on leave are '휴학 중'.

en: to move frequently; to move; to hop about

examples.ko: 그는 취직이 안 돼서 아르바이트를 전전했어요.
examples.en: He couldn't get a regular job and drifted from one part-time job to another.

examples.ko: 집값이 올라서 이 동네 저 동네를 전전하며 살았어요.
examples.en: House prices went up, so I lived moving from neighborhood to neighborhood.

examples.ko: 친구 집을 전전하는 생활도 이제 끝났어요.
examples.en: The life of hopping from one friend's house to another is over now.

examples.ko: 일자리를 전전하다 보니 한 곳에서 오래 일해 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: Because I kept hopping between jobs, I've never worked long in one place.
Even after going from hospital to hospital, I couldn't find the cause.
I still remember the days of moving from one rented room to another.

explain: 한곳에 머물지 못하고 여기저기 옮겨 다닌다는 뜻이고, 힘든 상황이라는 느낌이 있어요. '직장을 전전하다', '병원을 전전하다'처럼 목적어를 꼭 같이 써요. 일상에서는 '옮겨 다니다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.example: 어릴 때 이사를 자주 해서 여러 도시를 옮겨 다녔어요.
phrases.en: I moved a lot as a kid and went from city to city.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전전하다'와 같은 뜻의 쉬운 일상 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to say the same thing as '전전하다'.

phrases.example: 그는 몇 년 동안 직장을 전전했어요.
phrases.en: He drifted from job to job for several years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목적어 '직장을'과 함께 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation, used with the object '직장을'.
phrases.en_equiv: to drift from job to job

phrases.example: 어릴 때 친척 집을 전전하며 살았어요.
phrases.en: As a child, I lived moving from one relative's house to another.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'로 이어서 떠돌며 사는 생활을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses '-며' to describe a life of moving from place to place.

explain_en: To drift from place to place repeatedly, like jobs or cities. It means being unable to stay in one place and moving around, and it carries a feel of hard circumstances. It is always used with an object, as in '직장을 전전하다' or '병원을 전전하다'. In daily talk people also say '옮겨 다니다'.

examples.en: The gardener is trimming the rose bushes.
My father worked as a gardener for a long time.

examples.ko: 우리 집 정원은 정원사가 관리해 줘요.
examples.en: A gardener looks after our house's garden.
Thanks to the gardener, the yard became tidy.
I want to become a gardener someday.

examples.ko: 공원 정원사는 아침마다 꽃에 물을 줘요.
examples.en: The park gardener waters the flowers every morning.

explain: '요리사', '미용사'처럼 '사'가 붙은 직업 이름이에요. 집에서 취미로 가꾸는 사람은 보통 '정원사'라고 하지 않고 '정원을 가꾸다'라고 말해요. 일로 하는 사람이라는 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.en: My uncle works as a gardener in a park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업으로 하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it is someone's job.

phrases.en: I want to become a gardener later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about dreams or careers.

phrases.example: 전문 정원사가 나무를 예쁘게 잘라 줬어요.
phrases.en: A professional gardener trimmed the trees nicely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일로 하는 사람이라는 점을 더 분명히 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It makes clear the person does this as a profession.

explain_en: Person who tends gardens or parks, hired for upkeep. Like '요리사' and '미용사', the '사' ending marks a profession. Someone who gardens at home as a hobby is not usually called a '정원사'; people say '정원을 가꾸다' instead. The word carries a sense of doing it as a job.

t90.ax: I want to become a gardener someday.

examples.en: Which production company made this movie?
The production company announced a new drama.
My dream is to work at a big production company.
I emailed the game production company with a question.
The production company and the broadcaster signed a contract.

examples.ko: 제작사 이름은 영화가 끝날 때 나와요.
examples.en: The production company's name appears when the movie ends.

explain: 영화·드라마·음악·게임을 실제로 만드는 회사를 말해요. 방송을 내보내는 곳은 '방송사', 물건을 만드는 회사는 보통 '제조사'라고 해서 구별해요.

phrases.en: I work at a film production company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화를 만드는 회사를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a company that makes films.

phrases.example: 그 게임 제작사는 새 작품을 준비 중이에요.
phrases.en: That game company is preparing a new title.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임을 만드는 회사를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a company that develops games.

phrases.en: The production company announced its official position.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사의 입장을 전하는 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news about a company's statement.

explain_en: The company that makes a film, show or product. The company that actually makes a film, drama, music, or game. The one that airs it is the '방송사' (broadcaster), and a company that manufactures goods is usually a '제조사'.

en: to be devoted; to dedicate oneself

examples.en: I worked in the field of education for a long time.
My father works in agriculture.

examples.ko: 이 일에 종사하는 사람이 점점 줄고 있어요.
examples.en: The number of people working in this job is shrinking.
I went to university because I wanted to work in the medical field.
It's a job that requires a license to work in.

examples.ko: 서비스업에 종사한 지 십 년이 되었어요.
examples.en: It's been ten years since I started working in the service industry.

explain: '일하다'는 어디서나 쓰지만 종사하다는 분야나 업종에 써요. '교육에 종사하다'처럼 조사 '에'를 붙이고, 회사 이름 앞에는 쓰지 않아요. 직업을 소개하는 자리나 서류에서 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I work in the IT field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 어떤 분야에서 일하고 있다고 소개할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to introduce the field one currently works in.

phrases.example: 이 일의 종사자는 해마다 늘고 있어요.
phrases.en: The number of people working in this field grows every year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 분야에서 일하는 사람을 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for people who work in that field.

phrases.en: My parents work in agriculture.
phrases.nuance_ko: '분야나 업종 + 에'의 쓰임을 보여 주는 대표 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical collocation showing the 'field + 에' pattern.

explain_en: 일하다 works anywhere, but 종사하다 is for a field or industry. It takes the particle 에, as in '교육에 종사하다', and is not used with a company name. You often see it when introducing a career or on forms.

en: to take the lead; to take the initiative

examples.en: Minsu leads the meeting.
Our team took the lead on this event.
It's good when children take the lead in their own study.

examples.ko: 새로운 사업을 주도할 사람을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: We're looking for someone to lead the new business.
The one who drives the conversation is always my older sister.
He is leading the reform.

explain: '주도하다'는 앞장서서 이끌고 일이 가는 방향을 잡을 때 써요. '이끌다'보다 딱딱해서 회의, 사업, 대화, 개혁 같은 말과 자주 나와요. '학습을 주도하다'처럼 스스로 하는 모습에도 써요.

phrases.en: Minsu leads the team.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주도하다'보다 부드럽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer and more everyday than '주도하다'.

phrases.en: Our class takes the lead in the environmental campaign.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제일 먼저 나서서 한다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has the feel of stepping forward first.

phrases.en: Who is the person leading the conversation?
phrases.nuance_ko: '주도하는'으로 사람을 꾸미는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifier form describing a person.

explain_en: Take initiative and steer events, neutral tone. 주도하다 means to take the front and set the direction of something. It is more formal than 이끌다 and often goes with meetings, business, conversation and reform. It also fits self-directed things like '학습을 주도하다' (to lead one's own study).

gh: lead the way as a pioneer
lead an incident, often a bad one

p.n: 리드하다 is a casual loanword for guiding the flow; 주도하다 means taking charge.

en: to guide; to instruct; to coach

examples.en: The teacher guides the students' presentations.
I coached the juniors in the club.
The teacher who coaches exercise has come.
I'm grateful to the professor who advises my thesis.
You need patience when guiding children.
I have experience guiding students for a long time.

explain: 가르치고 이끄는 일이에요. '가르치다'는 지식을 전하는 것이고, '지도하다'는 방향을 잡아 주고 도와주는 느낌이 강해요. 명사 '지도'는 'map'과 소리가 같아서 문맥으로 구별해야 해요.

phrases.en: Teacher, please guide me with my presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도움과 방향을 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask for help and direction.

phrases.en: I receive guidance from my teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지도받는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person being guided.

phrases.en: The coach teaches kids soccer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지도하다'보다 일상에서 더 자주 쓰고 지식이나 기술을 전하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in daily life than 지도하다, with a sense of passing on knowledge or skill.

explain_en: Teacher or coach guides learners; supervises and instructs. It means teaching and leading. The plain verb for 'teach' passes on knowledge, while this one stresses setting a direction and helping along. The noun form sounds the same as the word for a map, so context tells them apart.

dis.h: teach or coach, like a teacher
gh: steer someone toward a desired result

p.n: Becomes showing the student around or giving information, not coaching.

t90.ax: I coached the juniors in the club.

examples.en: I'm studying geography at university.

examples.ko: 지리학 수업에서 지도 읽는 법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: In geography class, we learned how to read maps.
My older brother respects his geography professor.

examples.ko: 이번 학기에 지리학 수업을 두 개 들어요.
examples.en: I'm taking two geography classes this semester.
Geographers made a new map.
Geography has human geography and physical geography.

explain: 학교 과목은 '지리'이고, 대학에서 공부하는 학문은 '지리학'이에요. '지리학과', '지리학자'처럼 뒤에 붙는 말이 많아요. 인문지리와 자연지리로 크게 나눠요.

phrases.en: My older brother is in the geography department at university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학교의 학과 이름으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as the name of a university department.

phrases.en: A geographer studies the shape of mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지리학을 연구하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person who studies geography.

phrases.en: I majored in geography at university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학에서 학문으로 선택해 공부했다는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says you chose and studied it as an academic field.

explain_en: The school subject is 지리, while the university field is 지리학. Common extensions are 지리학과 (department) and 지리학자 (geographer). It splits mainly into human geography and physical geography.

en: to be recruited; to be hired; to be employed

examples.en: I was hired by a big company this year.
I did well in the interview and was hired right away.
New employees are usually hired in March.
The person who was hired starts work next week.
Can I be hired even without experience?
It's rare to be hired just by submitting documents.

explain: '뽑히다'는 말할 때 쓰는 편한 표현이고, '채용되다'는 공식적인 느낌이에요. 회사가 사람을 쓸 때 '채용하다'나 '뽑다'를 쓰고, 합격은 '붙다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The company hires new employees.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 쓰는 회사 쪽에서 말할 때 써요. '채용되다'와 짝이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the company's side as the one hiring. It pairs with 채용되다.

phrases.en: Out of ten people, only I was chosen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 편하게 쓰는 표현이에요. 면접이나 시험 뒤에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual spoken form, often used after an interview or exam.

phrases.en: I really hope I get hired this time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람을 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connected form used to express a wish.

explain_en: Passive — chosen and hired for a job (회사에 채용되다) '뽑히다' is the casual spoken form; '채용되다' sounds more official. A company says '채용하다' or '뽑다', and passing is also called '붙다'.

gh: called for or gathered, like members

p.n: 모집되다 doesn't fit a person getting hired; it is for the call for applicants.

t90.ax: I was hired by a big company this year.

examples.en: I think being a teacher is my true calling.

examples.ko: 그는 환자를 돌보는 일을 천직으로 여겨요.
examples.en: He regards caring for patients as his calling.

examples.ko: 이 일이 천직인지 아직 잘 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I'm still not sure whether this job is my calling.

examples.ko: 할머니는 평생 농사를 천직으로 알고 사셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother lived her whole life taking farming as her calling.
You work happily, like someone who has found their calling.

examples.ko: 요리사가 천직이라서 하루 종일 일해도 힘들지 않아요.
examples.en: Being a chef is my calling, so I'm not tired even after working all day.

explain: '직업'과 달리 나에게 딱 맞는 평생 할 일이라는 애정이 담겨 있어요. '천직으로 여기다', '천직으로 삼다', '천직이다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: She made writing her calling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 선택해서 평생 할 일로 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when one chooses something as a lifelong calling.

phrases.en: My father regarded farming as his calling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 일을 마음속으로 운명처럼 느낄 때 써서 '삼다'보다 마음가짐이 강조돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stresses the feeling of regarding the work as destiny, compared with 삼다.

phrases.en: I feel like I finally found my calling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자신에게 꼭 맞는 일을 찾았다는 기쁨을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses the joy of finding work that fits you perfectly.

explain_en: Unlike '직업' (job), it carries affection, meaning work that fits you perfectly and that you would do for life. It is used as '천직으로 여기다', '천직으로 삼다' or '천직이다'.
